_comment: SkyBlock drop name -> vanilla Minecraft item sprite, for the slot machine reels.
Every chance-based source the mod registers is covered, not only Diana. A settled reel
draws one of the event's own drops, so two drops from one event must never land on the
same sprite: three identical chests read as the machine having failed, and they empty
the three-of-a-kind flourish of meaning because every reel already matches. That is a
test rather than a hope -- DropSymbolsMcTest walks every source's jackpot list in
LootSourceRegistry, and every payout the simulator can roll, and fails when two
different rows share an item id and glint. Two spellings of one drop share one row and
are correctly ignored.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AS A RESOURCE. Hypixel renames things and adds drops between
updates. A player who sees a chest (the fallback) on a reel can drop a corrected copy of
this file into their resource pack, or a maintainer can fix it in a hotfix jar, without
anyone recompiling. com.skyprism.mc.symbols.DropSymbols reads it once, lazily, and caches
the resolved ItemStacks.
HOW A ROW IS CHOSEN. Where the SkyBlock wiki shows the drop reusing a vanilla texture
(most of them do), that vanilla item is used and 'why' says so. Where the drop has a
custom texture, the closest thing that still READS at 16x16 is used and 'why' argues the
case -- the test the choice has to pass is 'a player glancing at the reel half-recognises
the drop', not 'this is technically the same item'. Where a family of drops has no
vanilla counterpart at all, the family borrows one vanilla family that has enough members
to keep them apart: runes take pottery sherds, pets and sea creatures take spawn eggs,
vinyls take music discs, gemstones take the material of their own colour.
'glint': true adds the enchantment shimmer. SkyBlock draws every Enchanted <x> with a
glint, so mirroring that is what keeps Ancient Claw and Enchanted Ancient Claw -- both
flint -- apart on the reel, and likewise Hilt of Revelations and Daedalus Stick, both a
stick, and Fine and Flawless gemstones of one colour.
GLINT IS NOT AVAILABLE ON EVERY ITEM. Five ids used below already carry
enchantment_glint_override=true as a DEFAULT data component on both 26.1.2 and 26.2 --
enchanted_book, end_crystal, experience_bottle, nether_star and written_book -- so
'glint': true on one of those is a no-op and CANNOT separate two rows. That is a real bug
that shipped: the Grand and the Titanic Experience Bottle were one exp bottle apart by
glint alone, and they land on the same Ender Node, so the reel showed the same picture
twice. Two rows that share one of those five ids must never sit in one source's list.
'names' are display names as Hypixel writes them in chat. Matching is case-insensitive,
whitespace-collapsed, formatting-code-stripped, and ignores a leading or trailing count
('16x Ancient Claw', 'Enchanted Gold x16'), so only the base spellings belong here. A
trailing roman numeral is retried without it, so one 'Enchant Rune' row answers every
tier of it.
EVERY ITEM ID BELOW EXISTS IN BOTH MINECRAFT 26.1.2 AND 26.2 -- verified by dumping
BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.keySet() on each version's jar and intersecting, and again by
running DropSymbolsMcTest against both. Do not add an id without doing the same; a wrong
id is a missing-texture cube in the middle of the widget.
Drop tables read from https://hypixelskyblock.minecraft.wiki -- the Mythological Ritual
and Griffin Burrow pages on 2026-08-29, and the slayer, Catacombs, Kuudra, Crystal
Hollows, Glacite, fishing, foraging, Garden, Hoppity and Rift pages on 2026-08-30.
WHERE THE NAMES ARE CHECKED. Every name in this file is now pinned by
SkyBlockNameSnapshotTest against skyblock_item_names.tsv, a snapshot generated from the
NotEnoughUpdates item repository. A name that no longer resolves to a real SkyBlock item
fails the build, which is what "Chimera", "Enchanted Ancient Claws", "Soul Esperance" and
thirty-odd others needed and did not have -- they survived several review passes because
nothing checked. The handful of rows that legitimately name something that is not an item
(coins, chest tiers, the Carnival fruits) sit on that test's allowlist with a reason each.

Custom texture. Pointed dripstone is vanilla's barbed spike, which is what a manticore stinger is.
Custom texture. Its tooltip calls it 'an array of cells from different creatures mashed together'; the heart of the sea is vanilla's organic core sprite.

Wiki shows Enchanted_Yellow_Wool.png -- the golden fleece, shimmering, hence the glint.

The six Mythological attribute shards, all on the prismarine shard because they are one family and no source pays two of them in the reel-checked lists. Six invented shard names were removed from this row; these six are the only Diana shards that exist.
Not a burrow drop, but a Diana player's own tool turns up in chat capture and replays; the golden shovel is the spade.
Same reason as the feather it sheds.

Voidgloom Seraph's signature drop. Custom texture: a dark, faintly lit sliver. The echo shard is the only vanilla item drawn as a glowing splinter of something ancient, and it shares the drop's deep-teal cast.
Custom texture, a radiating point of void energy. The nether star is vanilla's only item drawn as a burst of light around a core, which is the atom silhouette exactly.

Custom texture: a violet power cell bristling with charge. An amethyst cluster is a bristling violet growth, and it is the one purple sprite in the Voidgloom table that is neither a shard nor a pearl.
A small device that burns mana continuously. The redstone torch is vanilla's always-on emitter, and its lit tip reads at 16x16 where a flat panel would not.
Vanilla's Warden grows its biome from the sculk catalyst, which is drawn as a dark bulb with a beating orange core -- a heart, from the creature the drop is named after.
A cosmetic skin. Hypixel serves skins as textured player heads, so the vanilla player head is not a lookalike, it is the same object class.
A goblet of blood. Vanilla owns no cup, but the potion is its only vessel drawn full of coloured liquid, and full is the half of the picture that matters.

Teleport hardware. The obvious choice was the eye of ender, and it was wrong: the wiki's Voidgloom Seraph table drops Summoning Eye out of the same fight, and Summoning Eye IS the vanilla eye of ender, so the two would have landed on one picture. The end crystal is the other End machine, it is violet and ringed like the Merger, and it is unclaimed.
A die. The quartz block is vanilla's only clean white cube at this size, which is the whole silhouette of a die; the Archfiend dice take the dark cubes so the three never collide.
The second die in the same drop table, so it must not be the white cube. A magma block is a cube lit from inside, in the red the Archfiend dice are drawn in.
The third die, and the lowest tier of the three. Crying obsidian is a dark cube with red veins: a die, dimmer than the High Class one.
Custom texture: a boxy appliance with a spout and a face. The blast furnace is vanilla's only front-loading machine sprite and reads as an appliance instantly.
A scythe head on a haft. Vanilla's hoe is the same long curved blade on a stick, which is why anything wanting a scythe reaches for it.
A Revenant Horror drop: torn undead tissue. Rotten flesh is that exact thing in vanilla.
A dismembered limb from the same zombie table. Vanilla has no hand, but the bone is its only severed-limb sprite and it cannot be confused with the flesh above it.
A severed zombie head. The vanilla zombie head is the same object.
A technical drawing. The filled map is vanilla's only sprite of a drawn plan rather than a blank sheet.
A device that inverts a Blaze Slayer's heat into cold. Blue ice is the coldest thing vanilla draws and the only one that reads as made rather than fallen.
Raw organs from the zombie boss. Raw porkchop is vanilla's unmistakably raw cut, and it is distinct from the rotten flesh already spoken for.
Spider silk. Vanilla string is spider silk dropped by spiders; the glinted form belongs to Braided Griffin Feather, so this stays plain.
Something small pulled half-dissolved out of a Tarantula Broodfather. The fermented spider eye is the only vanilla sprite that is both arthropod and visibly digested.
A flat paddle on a handle, which is what vanilla's wooden shovel is at 16x16 and what a swatter is at any size.
An egg. The plain vanilla egg, which keeps the four Goblin Eggs below free to be the coloured spawn eggs.
A tuner: a flat device that adjusts a signal passing through it. The comparator is vanilla's flat signal-adjusting device.

The catalysts are consumables that make a summon stronger, and the brewing stand is vanilla's apparatus for making something stronger. They get a row each rather than one shared row because the wiki's Tarantula Broodfather table pays Spider Catalyst and Tarantula Catalyst out of the same fight -- one row for the family would have put two reels on one picture.
Same family, different vessel; see Undead Catalyst. The empty bottle is the plainest of them, which suits the plainest catalyst.
Same family; this is the one that drops beside Spider Catalyst, so it takes the most potent-looking bottle vanilla has.

A brewed booster, so a bottle of something. The honey bottle is the only vanilla bottle left after the other catalysts took the brewing stand, the glass bottle and the dragon breath. Note this is not a Sven drop -- the wiki lists no catalyst on his table -- it is a bazaar item a player can still see in chat.

Runes are engraved tablets. Vanilla's pottery sherds are engraved tablets and come in twenty distinct engravings, which is what lets the rune family share one silhouette and still be different pictures. The prize sherd's motif is the closest to an enchanting sigil.
Same tablet family; the danger sherd's fanged motif is the one that reads as a snake.
Same tablet family; the burn sherd is literally a flame engraving.
Same tablet family; the howl sherd's open jaws are the bite.
Same tablet family; Couture is the decorative rune and the heart sherd is the decorative engraving.

The one rune that breaks the sherd convention on purpose: a note block says 'music' at 16x16 faster than any engraving could, and this one is a Garden visitor reward rather than a combat drop, so it never sits beside the others.
Byzantium is a deep purple, and vanilla's purple dye is both the sprite and the colour.
Matcha is a bright powdered green; lime is vanilla's brightest green pigment.
Brick red is red.
Celeste is a pale sky blue.
Flame is orange.
Necron's armour is black with red trim and the dye is drawn near-black. Black keeps it apart from the Livid dye it shares a dungeon chest with.
Livid's colour is the fight's own magenta, which is also the only magenta in the dungeon chest table.
Kuudra's tentacles are cyan, and cyan appears nowhere else in the Kuudra tables.
Pearlescent is an iridescent white; vanilla's white dye is the nearest pigment.
Bone is off-white grey. Light grey rather than white so it never doubles the Pearlescent dye.
The Hyperion's haft: a dark rod glowing along its length. The blaze rod is vanilla's glowing rod.

A scroll that teleports you through shadow. The ender pearl is vanilla's teleport, and it reads far faster than the three near-identical paper sprites the three Wither scrolls would otherwise have shared.
The second Wither scroll, and the one that detonates. TNT is the detonation.
The third Wither scroll, and it grants a shield. Vanilla's shield.
A heavy black greatsword. The netherite sword is vanilla's heaviest, darkest blade.
Drawn as an oversized pale-blue blade. The diamond sword is the pale-blue one, and it sits clear of the Claymore's netherite and the Fury's stone.
The third blade a Necron chest can pay, so it cannot repeat either of the two above. Stone is the greyest blade vanilla has, closest to the Fury's shadow-grey.
One row for all five stars, because they are the same star at five tiers and only one drops at a time. The nether star is a star dropped by a wither, which is the provenance exactly.
Wiki shows a wither skeleton skull, which is what they are made from and what vanilla calls the item.
The powder a wither is summoned over. Soul sand is that powder in vanilla, and it is not the skull directly above it.

Dungeon essence is the most common line in a reward chest and had no row, so it drew the fallback chest next to Necron's Handle and the Wither Catalyst. Custom texture in SkyBlock -- a pale glowing droplet, one tint per type. The ghast tear is vanilla's pale glowing droplet and is unused by any other row. One row answers every type because the reel cares that essence is not a chest, not which essence it was; the count that matters is already drawn as the xN.
Custom texture: a violet crystalline device. An amethyst cluster is the only violet crystalline sprite vanilla owns, and nothing else in a dungeon chest is purple.
An ancient machine's eye, cyan and ringed. The conduit is vanilla's ancient machine drawn as a ringed eye -- an unusually exact match for a custom texture.
A dark red dust used to forge wither gear. Redstone dust is vanilla's dark red dust.
A sceptre that fires bats of light. The breeze rod is a pale rod with light caught in it, and it stays clear of the blaze rod Necron's Handle holds.

entries.why: A scroll. Paper is a sheet with a destination written on it.
A gold accessory. The plain gold ingot is free -- Enchanted Gold holds the glinted one -- and it is the only gold in the Trapper table, so the ring and the coin payout never look alike.
A crest, so a small worn metal badge; the copper ingot is vanilla's only warm metal that the gold ingot (Hunter Ring) has not already taken.
A hunter's luck charm. The rabbit's foot is vanilla's luck charm, and the animal is what the Trapper sends you after.
A skinning knife: a short plain blade.
A soul, so the soul lantern -- a caged flame is the closest vanilla draws to a held soul.
A pearl. Vanilla's pearl.
A burning core. The fire charge is a contained burst of fire, and it is neither the magma cream nor the magma block used elsewhere.
A hunting shard off a sea creature. Prismarine is vanilla's undersea shard.
The second hunting shard in the same Kuudra chest, so a different shard: amethyst carries the dragon's violet.
A pearl, and the only one in the Kuudra tables.
Frozen Blaze armour is pale ice-blue, and diamond is the pale ice-blue armour.
A Great Spook keepsake drawn as a small blue-flamed light. The soul torch is that light.
A pickaxe. Diamond keeps it clear of the gold pickaxe and the axe the Scavenged tools hold in the same Divan tables.
The heart of the Jungle Temple, drawn as living green growth. The jungle sapling is the jungle in one sprite.
Vanilla's sniffer is its prehistoric animal and the sniffer egg is its prehistoric egg. The match is exact enough that no argument is needed.
A Goblin Egg is an egg you place to get a hostile humanoid, which is what a spawn egg is. The piglin's pink-red is the red one.
Same family as the Red Goblin Egg; the allay's blue is the blue one.

The four goblin eggs are colours, and each takes the spawn egg closest to its own: the frog egg is vanilla's green one. There is no golden or diamond goblin egg -- neither NEU nor Hypixel's own resource pack has one.
The bee egg is vanilla's yellow one; see Green Goblin Egg.
A graphics card: a flat board with a panel on it, which is exactly how vanilla draws the daylight detector.
A manufactured power core. The plain redstone block is a solid block of red power, and being plain it never doubles the glinted Enchanted Redstone Block the machine uses as filler.
A reflector: a panel with a bullseye that bounces a signal back. That is the target block.
A device that passes a signal on. The repeater is vanilla's signal relay.
A motor is the part that moves, and the piston is vanilla's moving part.
A gold mining tool dug out of the Mines of Divan. Gold names it, and the pickaxe head is what SkyBlock draws a hammer as.
Vanilla has this item exactly.
Vanilla has no emerald tool, so the gem itself carries it: green is the only thing separating this hammer from the golden one two rows up, and the gem is where the green is.
Vanilla has no lapis blade. The iron sword is the plain blade, and it is the only sword in the Metal Detector table, so no blue is needed to tell it apart.
A rope. The lead is vanilla's coiled rope.
Wiki shows a gold-trimmed helmet. Hypixel calls it "Yog Helmet"; ARMOR_OF_YOG_HELMET is only its internal name, which is what the mod used to print.
Mineral armour is crystalline pale blue, which is the diamond helmet.
SkyBlock's Lapis armour is blue-dyed leather, so the leather helmet is not a lookalike -- it is the same item, before the dye.
A torn scrap of a document. Paper is the sheet it was torn from.
Not an item at all -- the reward is the shaft opening -- so the reel shows the ice it opens in. Blue ice is the deepest, most deliberate-looking ice vanilla has.
Bone in a block of stone is what every fossil is. The five real fossils plus the two special ones; there is no "Rib Fossil" and no bare "Fossil".
A pale grey ingot. The plain iron ingot is free -- Enchanted Iron holds the glinted one -- and grey is the whole read.
Mithril is drawn in SkyBlock's own teal-green, and prismarine is the only teal-green material vanilla owns.
Compacted blue ice; packed ice is vanilla's compacted ice, plain, with Enchanted Packed Ice keeping the glinted form.
Stone that resists the pick. Andesite is the hardest-looking plain stone vanilla draws and is not the cobblestone its enchanted form uses.

A fish that is only bones. The bone is the bones.
Vanilla's own squid.
A shark pet. Vanilla has no shark, so the fish-shaped spawn eggs carry the sea pets, and cod is the plain grey one.
A sea pet; the tropical fish egg is the brightly coloured one, matching the pet's own colours.
A sea pet; the dolphin is vanilla's large blue swimmer.
A glowing orb pulled out of deep water, which is what the heart of the sea is.
A hunting shard off a freshwater creature; prismarine crystals are the pale water-blue shard, and the Kraken already holds prismarine's other form.
The second shard in the same treasure table, so a different one: quartz is a shard-shaped chip in a colour none of the others use.
A shed skin, which is what the phantom membrane is.
A vial of something you should not open. The ominous bottle is vanilla's sinister vial.

The other two thirds of a Lord Jawbus payout had no row at all, so a Jawbus reel drew the Radioactive Vial beside two identical chests -- the exact failure this file exists to stop, and the one the 2026-08-30 self-test frames still showed. A scute is a shell plate, which is the shape, and it is the only unused one. Its green is not the lava half of the name, but the reel is judged on telling three drops apart at 16x16 and green against the urchin's red is the widest separation available; checked on the captured frame rather than assumed. Deliberately not the nautilus shell, which reads as a shell more literally but is already Washed-up Souvenir's row and would collide inside the same fishing tables.

The third of the Jawbus payout, and the second chest in that frame. An urchin is a spiny sea growth; the fire coral fan is vanilla's spiny sea growth and its red-orange is the magma half of the name. Unused elsewhere, so it cannot collide with the scute beside it.
A piece of molten matter, which is magma cream.

A tooth, so the bone. There is no tierless "Shark Tooth Necklace" item -- every one of the five is its own item and Hypixel prints the tier, so all five are listed rather than a base name that would never match.
A fish, out of a tree. There is no vanilla sprite for the joke, so it takes the plain fish and lets the label underneath do the rest.
Attribute shards of a creature take that creature's spawn egg, which is the only vanilla family with enough members to keep them apart. The axolotl is vanilla's colour-changing lizard.
A root pulled from under a tree. Hanging roots are vanilla's roots.
Wiki shows an experience bottle. Boosters ship at a rarity and Hypixel prints it: the item is "Common Foraging Wisdom Booster", never the bare noun.
An axe booster, so the iron axe. Same rarity-prefix note as the wisdom booster.
Green sticky sap. The slime ball is green and sticky.
Wood. The oak log is wood.
Something that strengthens a signal on the way through -- the repeater, which shares nothing with the tree gift's other two rows.
The phantom spawn egg: Dreadwing is the Galatea phantom, and the shard is what actually drops -- the creature itself is not an item.
The polar bear spawn egg, vanilla's only bear. Kept as a row because the shard is real, but it is not on the phantom-tree table: the wiki's phantom creatures are Phanpyre, Phanflare and Dreadwing.
The allay spawn egg -- a small pale sprite of a creature. Same note as Grizzly Bear Shard: real item, not phantom-tree loot.
A green glow gathered off a tree. Glow lichen is the vanilla growth that glows green.
Spores from something fungal in the soil. The brown mushroom is the fungus.
Helianthus is the botanical genus of the sunflower, and vanilla ships the sunflower.
The fermented crop material, drawn as a dark purple mass. The fermented spider eye is vanilla's dark purple fermented thing and nothing else in the Garden tables uses it.
Wiki shows a nether wart. Plain, so the Mutant form stays distinct.
A chip that reads what is around it. The comparator is vanilla's reading device, and this is the only Garden crop drop that is hardware.
The first farming-armour material, drawn as harvested grain. Wheat is harvested grain.
The second farming-armour material, and a squash is a pumpkin.
A pest pet: a small green crawling blob, which is the slime.
A vinyl is a music disc. Vanilla has a dozen distinct disc sprites, which is what lets the three Garden vinyls be three different pictures instead of one repeated three times.
Second vinyl, second disc; see Wings of Harmony Vinyl.
Third vinyl, third disc; see Wings of Harmony Vinyl.
An overgrown nether wart. The block is the overgrown form, and using it rather than a glinted wart keeps it clear of Enchanted Nether Wart.

An enchantment, not an item: the Beetle pest drops it as an Enchanted Book, so the enchanted book is literally right. Both the tiered spelling Hypixel prints and the bare one are listed, because a trailing roman numeral is retried but a missing one is not.

Also an enchantment on an Enchanted Book, and it shares the Garden pest table with Pesterminator -- so it deliberately takes the knowledge book rather than the enchanted book, because two pest drops must not draw one picture. The mod used to call it "Ultimate Sunset", which is the internal id, not the name in chat.
A sealed dome worn on the head. The turtle helmet is vanilla's only domed, visorless headpiece, and no other Garden visitor reward is a helmet.
A key. Vanilla's trial key is a key.
A bunch of flowers on a stem, which is exactly the flowering azalea.
Grass that has grown too tall. Vanilla calls that tall grass.
Cloth tied round the head. The leather helmet is vanilla's dyeable cloth headpiece; the Space Helmet holds the hard-shell one, so the pair never repeats.
Wiki shows a pale blue shard. Prismarine crystals are vanilla's pale blue shard. Hypixel calls it "Fragmented Cryopowder"; CRYOPOWDER_SHARD is the internal name.
The Snow Suit is padded white cloth, which is dyed leather in vanilla terms.
The Snow Suit; see Snow Suit Helmet.
The Snow Suit; see Snow Suit Helmet.
The Snow Suit; see Snow Suit Helmet.
A star. The nether star is the star, and no Master Star is ever in a Winter Gift.
A cold blue amulet. The heart of the sea is vanilla's amulet sprite and its colour is right.
A splinter of ice. Prismarine's flat pale shard is the splinter, and the Talisman above it is a rounded amulet, so the pair reads apart at a glance.
Bait is a small fish on a hook in SkyBlock's own art, and the raw cod is the small fish.
A dyed cloth top. Leather is SkyBlock's cloth, and this is the only chest piece in the Frozen Treasure table.
Straight vanilla base item plus SkyBlock's enchanted shimmer.
A wrapped present. The red shulker box is a closed coloured box with a lid, which is the present -- and deliberately not a chest, because the chest is this table's own word for 'unknown'.
Half of a matched pair of jokes: this one is the fish, so it gets the fish.
A polished round medal. The clock is vanilla's only gold disc, and a token is a disc.
An exotic bright fruit, which is what glow berries are.
The Rift currency. A small purple spark, so the amethyst shard. Singular, because that is how Hypixel names the item; the plural is kept for the counted form.

A dark orb of void energy. The ender pearl is vanilla's dark orb, and it is the only one in the Voidgloom table.
Poison applied to an arrow, which is exactly what a tipped arrow is.
Same engraved-tablet family as the other runes; the flow sherd's swirl is the closest thing to a void motif, and it is the only sherd the Voidgloom table uses besides the Enchant rune's.
An upgrade you apply to a piece of gear. The smithing template is vanilla's upgrade-you-apply-to-a-piece-of-gear, down to the ornate border.

A figure carved out of end stone. The totem would have read better as an idol, but Diana's Minos Relic holds it; end stone is the material the name gives, and nothing else in the Voidgloom table is pale sandstone-yellow.
A pale wriggling grub. The silverfish is vanilla's pale wriggling thing, and its egg is the only sprite that shows one whole.
Same engraved-tablet family; the skull sherd is the grimmest engraving, which is the rune's whole tone.
A spider keepsake. Vanilla has no talisman, but the cobweb is unmistakably spider and nothing else in the Broodfather table is.
A vial of something that will hurt you. The ominous bottle is vanilla's sinister vial; the Spider Catalyst holds the plain bottle, so the two do not blur.
A hunting shard, and the only shard in the Broodfather table, so it takes the plain violet one.
Same engraved-tablet family; the friend sherd is the warm one, which suits the wolf rune.
A ball of fur. Rabbit hide is vanilla's loose fur.
A salmon. The Grizzly Bait in the same table is a cut of red meat, so the two stay apart.
A wheeled contraption an animal runs in. The minecart is vanilla's only wheels-and-frame sprite.
Same engraved-tablet family; the mourner sherd is the one with tears on it.

names: Wisp's Ice-Flavored Water I Splash Potion
entries.why: It is a splash potion. The Blaze Catalyst in the same table is the cauldron, so nothing repeats.
Arrows. Vanilla's arrow, plain, with the Twilight Arrow Poison keeping the tipped one.
Books that have been through a fire. The written book is the only bound book vanilla draws that is not the enchanted one, which the Inferno table also pays.
A hunting shard, and the only shard in the Inferno table.
The lesser of the two cold inverters the Inferno Demonlord pays. Plain ice, with Subzero Inverter taking blue ice, so a boss that drops both shows two pictures.
The five Distillates are one bottled essence per ingredient and several can drop at once, so each takes the ingredient it was distilled from. This one is the blaze rod, ground.
The glowstone one; see Blaze Rod Distillate.
The magma cream one; see Blaze Rod Distillate.
The nether wart one; see Blaze Rod Distillate.
Gabagool is cured pork, so the cooked porkchop; see Blaze Rod Distillate.
A crystal that holds power. The end crystal is vanilla's power-holding crystal, and the Etherwarp Merger that shares it is a Voidgloom drop, never an Inferno one.
A key. The tripwire hook is vanilla's hooked metal shape and reads as a key at 16x16; the trial key is already the Jungle Key.
The same key, hotter: the ominous trial key is the orange-lit variant of the sprite the plain key family uses.
Cyclamen is a pink flower; the pink dye is the pink one.
A fire wand. The blaze rod is vanilla's burning stick.
It freezes, and the snowball is the only vanilla sprite that reads as thrown cold at 16x16 without taking the ice the Glacite rows use.
A great axe. The golden axe is the only axe left after the diamond one went to the Scavenged Diamond Axe.
Glowing fibre; the glow ink sac is vanilla's glowing loose material.
A skull. The wither skeleton skull is already the Master Skull family, so this takes the plain one.
A fang: a long pale spike. Pointed dripstone is vanilla's spike.
Arachne's armour is a four-piece set, so it takes a whole vanilla armour family that nothing else in this table had claimed.
See Arachne's Helmet.
See Arachne's Helmet.
See Arachne's Helmet.
An attribute shard, and the amethyst shard is the sprite this table already uses for a purple fragment.
A spool of thread; the vanilla string is thread.
A geode: crystals in a shell, which is exactly the vanilla amethyst block.
End stone, glinted like every Enchanted <x>.
It is an experience bottle.

The bigger one, and it cannot use the experience bottle the Grand bottle has: minecraft:experience_bottle carries enchantment_glint_override=true as a DEFAULT component on 26.1.2 and 26.2, so "glint": true on it changes nothing and the two bottles landed on one picture. Dragon breath is the nearest vanilla bottle that is visibly a different silhouette, and it is End-flavoured, which is where the Ender Node is.
One of the named fish, and the tropical fish is vanilla's only sprite that reads as a special fish rather than dinner.
The gifts are wrapped boxes and the shulker boxes are vanilla's only wrapped boxes, one per colour.
See White Gift.
Scriptures, so a book; the written book is already Scorched Books.
Iceberg is deep blue.
Aquamarine is blue-green; the cyan dye is blue-green.

The Great Spook candies are flat coloured sweets with no vanilla counterpart at all; dye powder is the only 16x16 sprite that reads as a small thing of one colour, and the three candies need three colours that stay apart.
See Green Candy.
See Green Candy.
An alloy ingot; the netherite ingot is vanilla's alloy.
A pet item that is a claw on a foot; the rabbit foot is the vanilla foot.
A green gem. It shares the plain emerald with the Fine Jade Gemstone row, which is a different content area, and stays clear of the glinted emerald the Flawless jade takes on its own table.
A cut jewel. The plain diamond was free -- Enchanted Diamond is the glinted one.
A tool handle with a jewel in it; the golden hoe is the only vanilla haft left in this table.
A scute. The turtle scute is already the Lava Shell, so this takes the armadillo one.
A light in a cage, which is what a lantern is.
A small hinged metal disc worn on a chain; the compass is vanilla's only such object.
Cereal made of tiny metal bits, which is what a pile of gold nuggets looks like.
A carved standing figure; the armour stand is vanilla's standing figure.
One of the named fish.
See White Gift; the gold one takes the yellow box.
A sack. The bundle is vanilla's sack.
A dark horned helmet. It has to differ from the Snow Suit Helmet it shares the gift table with, so it takes chainmail rather than leather.
Holly berries are red.
Thunder, so the lightning rod.
A small silver thing; the iron nugget is vanilla's small silver thing, and the magma cream is already the Magma Lord Fragment it shares a table with.
A sea-creature attribute shard, and prismarine is vanilla's sea material.
A skull worn as a trophy; the player head is vanilla's worn head.
Soft boots. Leather is the soft vanilla boot, and the Snow Suit that also uses it is a different table.
Carmine is a dark red-brown, and the plain red dye is already spoken for twice over.
A creature shard takes that creature's spawn egg; the parrot is vanilla's small bright bird.
One of the three phantom-tree creatures; the bat is vanilla's night flier.
The burning one of the three; the blaze is vanilla's burning flier.
Eyes. The vanilla spider eye is an eye.
Pale grubs in a crop, which at 16x16 is what a scatter of seeds looks like.
A soft wriggling blob; the slime ball is the vanilla blob.
A torn wing, which is what the phantom membrane is.
A hooked chip of something hard; the flint is the shape this table already uses for the Ancient Claw, on a different island.
Contained fire, which is what the fire charge is.
A thing that makes a noise when you hit it.
It is a book.
A small green leaf spray. The fern is vanilla's.
The upgraded clover, glinted so it stays apart from the plain one it shares the visitor table with.
A minion skin is a head, and the player head is the head.
Wild strawberry is pink.
It is a poppy.
A small bright pinned disc; the firework star is the closest vanilla draws to a badge.

The eight Carnival fruits are a real dig table the wiki lists, but none of the seven besides Dragonfruit exists in the NEU item database, so each borrows the closest vanilla fruit. The golden apple is vanilla's yellow-orange one.
A brown tropical pod; see Mango.
It is an apple.
Small red fruit; see Mango.
A dark red round fruit; see Mango.
The spiky one; see Mango.
It is a melon. The glinted melon slice is Enchanted Melon, so this takes the plain one.

A tooth, so the bone -- and it is free on the Sven Packmaster table, where the other bone rows (Severed Hand, Skeleton Fish) do not appear. It went in when the published Sven table was corrected: the wiki lists Wolf Tooth, and lists no catalyst at all.
